summary: Zubayr ibn al-Awwam accepted Islam early and was the Prophet's ﷺ cousin. He was one of the ten companions promised Paradise. He was a fierce warrior who fought in every major battle and was the first to draw his sword in defense of Islam.

title: The Year of the Elephant
summary: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant (570 CE). This was the year Abraha, the Abyssinian governor of Yemen, marched on Makkah with an army including an elephant to destroy the Kaaba. Allah destroyed the army with flocks of birds dropping stones of baked clay.

title: The Orphan's Childhood
summary: Muhammad ﷺ was born an orphan, his father passing away before his birth. His mother Aminah passed away when he was six, leaving him in the care of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, and then his uncle Abu Talib. He grew up with a pure character, known as As-Sadiq (The Truthful) and Al-Amin (The Trustworthy).

title: The Marriage to Khadijah
summary: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a successful and noble businesswoman, hired Muhammad ﷺ to trade for her. Impressed by his honesty and character, she proposed marriage. He was 25 and she was 40. Their marriage was one of profound love, support, and mutual respect.

title: The First Revelation
summary: Muhammad ﷺ would retreat to the cave of Hira to reflect. During one of these retreats, the Angel Jibril appeared and commanded him to 'Read'. After the third command, Muhammad ﷺ asked what he should read, and Jibril taught him the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq.

title: The Early Call
summary: After the first revelation, the Prophet ﷺ began calling people to Islam secretly for three years. The first to believe were his wife Khadijah, his cousin Ali, his friend Abu Bakr, and his adopted son Zayd. He then received the command to call publicly.

title: The Persecution Begins
summary: As the message of Tawhid spread, the Quraysh leaders felt threatened. They began persecuting the Muslims, especially the poor and enslaved, torturing them to renounce their faith. Bilal, Ammar, and Sumayyah were among those who suffered greatly.

title: The Migration to Abyssinia
summary: Due to severe persecution, the Prophet ﷺ advised some Muslims to migrate to Abyssinia (Ethiopia). The Christian king, Negus, was known for his justice. The Muslims were welcomed, and when the Quraysh tried to demand their return, Negus refused to hand them over.

title: The Boycott of Banu Hashim
summary: The Quraysh imposed a social and economic boycott on the Prophet's clan, Banu Hashim. They were forced into a valley for three years, facing severe hunger and hardship. The boycott ended when sympathetic Quraysh members tore up the agreement.

title: The Year of Sorrow
summary: The Prophet ﷺ faced immense grief when his beloved wife Khadijah passed away, followed shortly by his protective uncle Abu Talib. This year was known as the Year of Sorrow (Am al-Huzn). The Prophet ﷺ faced increased hostility from the Quraysh after their deaths.

title: The Night Journey
summary: The Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Isra and Mi'raj, a miraculous night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem, and then through the heavens. He met previous prophets and received the command for the five daily prayers directly from Allah, bringing comfort after the Year of Sorrow.

title: The Pledges of Aqabah
summary: The Prophet ﷺ met with delegations from the tribes of Madinah at Aqabah. They pledged their allegiance to him and invited him to migrate to their city. These pledges laid the foundation for the establishment of the Muslim community in Madinah.

title: The Hijrah
summary: After years of persecution in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ received permission to migrate to Madinah. He left with Abu Bakr, hiding in the cave of Thawr for three days. They made the journey to Madinah, establishing the first Islamic state and a new era in history.

title: The Building of the Masjid
summary: Upon arriving in Madinah, the first act the Prophet ﷺ performed was building a mosque (Masjid an-Nabawi). It became the center of worship, education, and governance. The Prophet ﷺ participated in the construction, carrying bricks alongside his companions.

title: The Constitution of Madinah
summary: The Prophet ﷺ established a constitution that united the diverse tribes of Madinah, including the Muhajirun, Ansar, and Jewish tribes. It guaranteed freedom of religion and established rules for mutual defense and cooperation, creating a unified society.

title: The Battle of Badr
summary: The Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH, where 313 poorly equipped Muslims faced an army of 1,000 Quraysh. Despite the odds, the Muslims fought with immense faith, and Allah sent angels to strengthen them. The Muslims won a decisive victory, establishing their strength.

title: The Battle of Uhud
summary: In 3 AH, the Quraysh sought revenge at Uhud. The Muslims initially had the upper hand, but some archers disobeyed orders, leaving a flank exposed. The Quraysh counter-attacked, and many Muslims were martyred, including Hamza. The Prophet ﷺ himself was injured.

title: The Battle of the Trench
summary: In 5 AH, a massive confederacy of tribes attacked Madinah. Acting on Salman al-Farsi's advice, the Muslims dug a deep trench (Khandaq) around the city. The siege lasted weeks, but the enemy was unable to breach the trench and eventually retreated.

title: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
summary: The Prophet ﷺ set out for Umrah, but the Quraysh blocked his path at Hudaybiyyah. A treaty was signed, appearing unfavorable to the Muslims but containing terms of peace for 10 years. The Quran called this a clear victory, as it allowed Islam to spread peacefully.

title: The Conquest of Makkah
summary: In 8 AH, after the Quraysh broke the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet ﷺ marched to Makkah with an army of 10,000 Muslims. The Quraysh surrendered. The Prophet ﷺ entered with humility, cleansed the Kaaba of idols, and forgave his former enemies.

title: The Battle of Hunayn
summary: After the conquest of Makkah, the Hawazin and Thaqif tribes gathered to attack the Muslims at Hunayn. The Muslims initially faced a setback due to the large number of new converts relying on their numbers. However, the Prophet ﷺ rallied them, and the Muslims won a decisive victory.

title: The Farewell Sermon
summary: During his final Hajj, the Prophet ﷺ delivered a powerful sermon on the plains of Arafah to over 100,000 Muslims. He proclaimed the sanctity of life and property, abolished racism and usury, and emphasized the rights of women. He revealed the final verse of the religion's completion.

title: The Passing of the Prophet
summary: After a brief illness, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away in Madinah in 11 AH, at the age of 63. His death was a profound loss for the Ummah, but Abu Bakr reminded them that Allah is Ever-Living and never dies. He was buried in the room of Aisha.

title: The Shahada
summary: The Shahada is the declaration of faith: 'La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur rasulullah' (There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His messenger). It is the first and most important pillar of Islam, representing a complete submission to the oneness of God.

title: The Five Daily Prayers
summary: Salah is the second pillar of Islam and the direct connection between a servant and Allah. Muslims are required to pray five times a day: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha. Prayer involves physical movements, specific recitations, and deep focus.

title: Wudu (Ablution)
summary: Wudu is the ritual purification required before performing the prayer. It involves washing the hands, rinsing the mouth, cleaning the nose, washing the face, arms, wiping the head, and washing the feet. It is a physical and spiritual act of cleansing that prepares the believer for prayer.

title: Fasting in Ramadan
summary: Fasting (Sawm) during Ramadan is the fourth pillar of Islam. It involves abstaining from food, drink, and marital relations from dawn to sunset. The purpose of fasting is to develop taqwa (God-consciousness), practice self-discipline, and feel empathy for the poor.

title: Zakat (Charity)
summary: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam, an obligatory charity of 2.5% of a Muslim's saved wealth over a certain threshold each year. It purifies wealth, protects society, and helps the poor, the needy, and the debtors. All wealth belongs to Allah.

title: Hajj (Pilgrimage)
summary: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam, an obligatory pilgrimage to Makkah for those who are physically and financially able at least once in their lifetime. It involves rites such as Tawaf, Sa'i, and standing at Arafah. Hajj demonstrates equality and devotion.
